cover_headline: Republican Bill Would Raise H-1B Exemption Threshold to Nearly $140,000
facts: The bill would replace the $60,000 salary exemption, unchanged since 1998, with twice the National Average Wage Index — nearly $140,000 today
The figure is not a minimum H-1B salary, and the master's-degree exemption would remain
The House bill, H.R. 10799, sits in the Judiciary Committee, and the proposal has no immediate effect on H-1B petitions or extensions

quote.text: For decades, companies have been able to sidestep hiring American workers because of a salary threshold that hasn't budged since 1998. That's not modernization, that's a loophole.
quote.speaker: Jon Husted

end.headline: Republican Bill Would Raise H-1B Exemption Threshold to Nearly $140,000
end.line: House and Senate versions of the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would tie the exemption to twice the national average wage instead of the $60,000 figure set in 1998.
